submission.justification: Absorber-F2 gave the best resolution in every comparison. At 5 mm it reached 3.21% at 100 GeV, which is the minimum of my F2 scan. The scan gave 3.82% at 2 mm, 3.32% at 4 mm, 3.21% at 5 mm, 3.28% at 6 mm and 3.69% at 8 mm. F3 gave 4.29% at 2 mm and 3.91% at 4 mm. F1 gave 5.84% at 2 mm. The 2025 summary at 5 mm ranks the materials the same way: F2 3.2%, F3 3.9%, F1 5.1%. I did not simulate F3 or F1 at every thickness, so their optimum thicknesses are extrapolated from the trend. Caveat: none of the documents give activation or radiation-protection data for these materials. I could not verify that the hands-on maintenance constraint is met for the dense alloys, and F1, the standard structural material, is the likeliest to be compatible. Please confirm F2's activation properties before finalizing. If F2 fails that check, F3 is the next-best choice at about 4 mm.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: F2 at 5 mm gives 3.21%, the best of all simulated configurations. F3 gave 3.91% at best and F1 5.84% at 2 mm.

requirements.requirement: Absorber is one of the three candidate materials
